questions.q: What is syslog, and what kind of systems typically use it to send logs?
options: The standard logging protocol used by Unix/Linux systems and most network devices like firewalls, routers, and switches
A Windows-only service for reading the Security log
A file format for storing screenshots of log data
A proprietary protocol that only one firewall vendor supports
questions.explain: Syslog originated on Unix systems and is now the default logging language of Linux servers and nearly every network appliance.

questions.q: In a syslog message, what does the leading value like <34> represent?
options: The PRI value, calculated as facility times 8 plus severity
The exact port number the message was sent over
A random message ID with no defined meaning
The number of characters in the message body
questions.explain: The PRI value encodes both the facility and the severity in a single number, letting a SIEM classify the message before parsing its text.

questions.q: On the syslog severity scale, which level represents the MOST severe condition?
options: 0, Emergency
7, Debug
4, Warning
They are all equally severe
questions.explain: Syslog severity runs from 0 (Emergency, most severe) down to 7 (Debug, least severe).

questions.q: Why did vendors adopt formats like CEF and LEEF on top of plain syslog?
options: Raw syslog only standardizes the envelope, not the message body, so CEF/LEEF give the body a standardized key-value structure any SIEM can parse
Because syslog cannot be sent over a network at all
Because CEF and LEEF replace syslog's transport protocol entirely
Because severity levels only exist in CEF, not in syslog itself
questions.explain: CEF and LEEF standardize the key-value content inside the message so one parser works across many vendors' products.

questions.q: In the CEF line src=203.0.113.55 dst=10.0.0.5 spt=51413 dpt=22, what does dpt represent?
options: The destination port
The device priority type
The data packet total
The daily processing time
questions.explain: CEF's key-value fields use dpt for destination port and spt for source port, alongside src and dst for the IP addresses.
